hints.title: Suffix Accumulation Inversion
hints.text: The first character is shifted by all shifts combined, the second by all shifts from index 1 onward, and so on. Working backwards accumulates the required shift for each position directly.

hints.title: Modulo Suffix Sum Invariant
hints.text: Because shifting twenty-six times completes a full alphabet circle, accumulating suffix sums modulo twenty-six prevents large integer overflow.

hints.title: Reverse Cumulative Shift Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a cumulative shift variable to zero. Iterate backwards from the last index to zero. Add shifts[i] to cumulative shift and take modulo twenty-six. Shift character s[i] forward by that cumulative amount wrapping around lowercase z. Reverse and join or directly construct the resulting string.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Applying each shift sequentially across all prefix elements takes O(N^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Computing suffix sums from right to left takes O(N) time and requires O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output string.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that prefix updates are equivalent to suffix accumulations modulo 26.
